title: The Reformation of the World as Overseen by a Realist Demon King
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Reincarnated in another world as Astaroth, the 72nd and weakest demon king, a man from our world sets out to unite the land under his rule. Using knowledge from his past life, he applies cold strategy: striking heroes before they grow strong, wrecking enemy economies with counterfeit money and modernizing his forces. Summoned servants, including Eve, join him as he builds his realm and challenges rival demon kings.
life_message: Clear-eyed strategy and results matter more than tradition or chivalry when building a realm.

content.note: War between demon kings and against heroes (AniList War; MU blurb: cannons against werewolves). Cap at 3 (to verify gore).
Zombies and demons (AniList); tone praised as fun (Siliconera).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Opens with a challenge to another demon king 'for glory and power' (Siliconera), but strategy beats pride.

Order vs freedom.evidence: A centralized realm reformed from the top.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty runs to subjects and summoned servants, not family.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Demon king and summoned servants (MU Master-Servant Relationship).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Old tendencies are 'reformed' by past-life knowledge (MU blurb).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival of the weakest demon king drives every choice.

folkways.japan: The rational reformer bringing modern methods to a feudal world echoes Japan's own Meiji modernization story, a frequent theme in kingdom-building isekai.

delivery.evidence: Siliconera praises clever plotting; choices 'strategically brilliant' but not moral; no comment on preachiness.
delivery.note: The protagonist's amoral pragmatism is presented as clever and effective, and traditional heroics appear mainly as something he outmaneuvers.

winners_losers: Astaroth's realism wins; rival demon kings and heroes who follow convention lose.
